review_text: This place had a very pleasing vibe. It was my first time to dine, and it was a good experience. Their food was good. Some of the dishes were a bit bland for my preference, but was still good. The serving size was very good for their price, too. Service wise, their serving time was fast. While it could be because it was afternoon when we went, but we didn't have to wait for so long. There were multiple seats available, and the atmosphere was really great. Could use some music, like jazz or elevator music, but otherwise, still good setting.

> One thing that really amazed me and made me want to come back is the friendliness of the staff. I don’t know his name, but I can still recognize his face. He was very accommodating and even gave me a tour of the place. > I also love the ambiance—it’s very clean and well-organized. The food tastes healthy and doesn’t seem loaded with MSG or synthetic seasonings. As a health advocate, I truly appreciate this. I highly recommend their restaurant, especially the halo-halo. It isn’t overly sweet or harsh on the throat; it has just the right level of sweetness that I can enjoy. > The prices are reasonable, and I’m looking forward to coming back with my friends. I can’t wait to experience their KTV bar I’d love to sing gospel songs there. I also appreciate that this café is God-centered. I noticed Bible verses on their shirts, and I learned that they also conduct Sunday services. I hope to attend one someday.

Pros: The ambiance is great. Feels cozy and homey. Service staff are attentive and polite. Cons: Food is too sweet. Even the sisig and pares were too sweet. It's like everything we ate had sugar in it. Less sweet and more salt on the food, would be 5 stars. Decent experience overall. Might come back to try their coffee.

I am writing this review directly from the venue to express my deep disappointment with the service at Yukiss Cafe & Events Room. We arrived at exactly 10:00 PM. The doorman/guard (the guy wearing a red-striped shirt) was very polite and greeted us well. However, the energy completely shifted once we stepped inside. There were three staff members at the counter: a young man and two women, one of whom was older. They all had frowns on their faces, looking completely unhappy to see customers. They initially handed us the menu, but just as we were about to order, they abruptly informed us that they were already closing. We pointed out that according to Google and Facebook, their operating hours are until 1:00 AM. However, they told us that they actually close at 11:40 PM. I politely asked the older woman for an explanation regarding this discrepancy, asking, "Ano masasabi mo, ma'am?" (What can you say about this, ma'am?). She completely ignored me and gave no response. Despite saying they were closing, they still let us order. Since we traveled all the way here—and the location is quite hidden, dark to get into, and exhausting to reach—we didn't want our effort to go to waste. We originally planned to sing videoke and order ramen, but our mood was completely ruined. We ended up just ordering 4 Smirnoff Mules because of the pressure that they were closing, even though we could still hear other customers singing videoke. To make matters worse, the older woman audibly remarked, "Nag sayo unta mo" (You should have come earlier). It felt like a joke because they were making it seem like it was our fault, which was shocking. Less than two drinks in—not even halfway through our beverages—they immediately demanded payment because they needed to do a "cash count." There was absolutely no consideration for the customers. When we left, there was no "thank you" or even a simple "pasensya po" (we're sorry) from that older woman. As someone who understands the food industry, I completely get that they were exhausted and wanted to go home. I know how hard the job is, and I would have gladly understood if they just handled us properly. In fact, I kept smiling and even made light jokes to keep things light. I handled myself nicely, but the treatment I got in return was just rude. What hurts the most is that I brought my family with me. To have my family go through such a terrible and unwelcoming experience really hurts on my part. The way they practically shooed us away proved they have zero knowledge of customer service. The staff badly needs a seminar on hospitality and how to speak politely to paying customers. To be fair, the doorman in the red stripes was courteous. The young male staff member, who was clearly forced by the two women to collect our payment early, was also polite to us. Meanwhile, the two female staff members hid and ducked behind the counter out of embarrassment. The embarrassment is real. The place itself is beautiful, well-designed, and aesthetic. It is clear that the owner invested a lot of thought, money, and effort into the decorations and details. It’s such a pity that a great business is being ruined by the terrible attitude of its employees. Looking at other Google reviews, it seems I am not alone—most complaints are about the staff. I truly feel bad for the owner if they are unaware of how their employees are sabotaging their investment. Pros: Beautiful aesthetic, polite doorman, and polite young male staff. Cons: Horrible customer service from the female staff, inconsistent operating hours, and very rude, dismissive behavior towards families.
